target_name: Two Sided Payout Deviation From Own Norm
rationale: The construction is internally coherent (positive deviations weighted by cheapness, negative by richness, consistent with a positive sign) and pairs the archive's best structural template with its best-Sharpe measurement, but it is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested archive components rather than a new mechanism, so its incremental information is limited to whether the two-sided weighting generalizes.

target_name: Rising Payout Long Rising Raising Short
rationale: This is the most substantive proposal in the batch — it replaces the short leg's variable rather than reweighting it, the sign algebra checks out (rich firms with rising gross raising receive a negative contribution), and it directly tests whether the short side is about market dependence rather than the negative tail of a netted flow; the main risk is double-loading of firms that both pay out and raise.

target_name: Standardized Payout Trend Beyond Earnings Trend
rationale: This is a monotone rescaling of an existing archive signal, and the archive already contains a common-scale differenced version of exactly this idea ("Payout Unusual Beyond The Earnings Cycle", fmb 1.11, alpha 0.020) whose weak result undercuts the claimed scale-mismatch diagnosis; the change is cosmetic rather than economic.

target_name: Two Sided Trajectory Against Multiple Path
rationale: Sign logic and construction are sound and the both-legs-as-paths framing is a genuinely untried configuration, but like proposal one it is a template-times-base recombination of two archived results, and the earnings-yield trend leg risks becoming a disguised multi-year price-reversal bet rather than a valuation state.

target_name: Debt Repayment Trajectory At Cheap Value
rationale: A clean and diagnostically valuable decomposition — it isolates the debt half of the combined flow whose shareholder half already tested weakly, so either outcome is informative about the mechanism, though it edges toward the well-known debt-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly and the five-point trend on lumpy dltr/dltis will be noisy.

Acceleration is the one untested temporal object in this family and the hypothesis is coherent, but second differences of a lumpy annual payout flow are very noisy, and the claimed coverage gain over the five-year trend is asserted without justification and may not materialize.
